root_cause.text: The `xfs_alloc_buftarg()` function fails to release the DAX device reference acquired during initialization when an error occurs in the error path, causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `fs_put_dax(btp->bt_daxdev, mp);` to the `error_free:` label in `xfs_alloc_buftarg()`. This call was missing despite the function acquiring a DAX device reference (introduced in commit 6f643c57d57c). Without this cleanup, the reference count on the DAX device is not decremented when the function returns an error, leaving the resource unreleased.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by releasing DAX device reference in error path of xfs_alloc_buftarg.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `fs_put_dax(btp->bt_daxdev, mp)` in the error_free label of the xfs_alloc_buftarg function, before the kfree(btp) call.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when xfs_alloc_buftarg fails and jumps to the error_free label, the DAX device reference held in btp->bt_daxdev is properly released back to the filesystem before the buffer target structure itself is freed. Without this, the DAX device reference would leak, preventing proper cleanup and potentially causing resource exhaustion or use-after-free issues.

candidates.rationale: This line in the error path fails to release the DAX device reference that was acquired during xfs_alloc_buftarg() initialization. The function acquires a DAX device reference but only frees the buffer target structure (btp) without calling the corresponding release function for the DAX device, causing a resource leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement at line 1759 in the error path of xfs_alloc_buftarg() frees the buffer target structure but fails to release the DAX device reference that was acquired during initialization. The function acquires a DAX device reference (likely via dax_get_by_host() or similar) but the error path only calls kfree(btp) without the corresponding dax_put_device() or equivalent release function, causing a resource leak of the DAX device reference.

Author: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>

    xfs: convert remaining kmem_free() to kfree()
    
    The remaining callers of kmem_free() are freeing heap memory, so
    we can convert them directly to kfree() and get rid of kmem_free()
    altogether.
    
    This conversion was done with:
    
    $ for f in `git grep -l kmem_free fs/xfs`; do
    > sed -i s/kmem_free/kfree/ $f
    > done
    $
    
    Si
